examples.question_text: In a sports club, $27$ members play basketball, $21$ play volleyball and $9$ play both. How many members play basketball or volleyball?
A gym has $140$ members. $86$ use weights and $97$ use cardio equipment. Every member uses at least one type of equipment. How many use both?
examples.solution_text:
Let $W$ represent weights and $C$ represent cardio. Every member belongs to the union, so $|W\cup C|=140$.

$\begin{aligned}|W\cup C|&=|W|+|C|-|W\cap C|\\140&=86+97-|W\cap C|\\140&=183-|W\cap C|\\|W\cap C|&=43\end{aligned}$

$43$ members use both.

examples.question_text: A survey of $72$ music students found that $43$ play piano, $14$ play both piano and guitar, and $9$ play neither. How many play guitar?
examples.solution_text:
Let $P$ represent piano and $G$ represent guitar. Subtract those who play neither to find the union.

$|P\cup G|=72-9=63$.

$\begin{aligned}|P\cup G|&=|P|+|G|-|P\cap G|\\63&=43+|G|-14\\63&=29+|G|\\|G|&=34\end{aligned}$

$34$ students play guitar.

examples.question_text: In a group of $45$ students, $19$ travel to school by bus and $26$ walk. Each student uses exactly one of these methods. Let $B$ represent bus travel and $W$ represent walking. Find $|B\cup W|$.
A survey found that $|A|=37$, $|B|=29$ and $|A\cap B|=12$. Find the number in $A$ only, $|A\cap B'|$.
In a class of $40$ students, $24$ study German and $19$ study French. $6$ study neither language. Find the numbers who study (a) German only and (b) French only.
In a group of $60$ students, $31$ study Art, $26$ study Music and $11$ study both. How many study neither Art nor Music?

examples.solution_text:
Each set total includes the overlap.

$\begin{aligned}|A|&=14+6\\&=20\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}|B|&=11+6\\&=17\end{aligned}$

The overlap contains $6$ elements. Apply the inclusion–exclusion rule.

$\begin{aligned}|A\cup B|&=|A|+|B|-|A\cap B|\\&=20+17-6\\&=31\end{aligned}$

Adding the three regions inside the circles also gives $14+6+11=31$.
